findings.claim: Elite distance runners and cyclists often practise glycogen loading... Dina Asher-Smith, for example, works carefully with nutritionists to ensure her glycogen stores are fully loaded before major championships.
findings.truth: Asher-Smith is a 100 m and 200 m sprinter. Sprint events are fuelled by ATP-PC and anaerobic glycolysis, not by loaded glycogen stores, so she is the wrong illustration for an endurance strategy. Replaced with a marathon runner.
findings.evidence: Wikipedia, Dina Asher-Smith (sprinter); standard glycogen-loading physiology

findings.claim: Carbohydrate is the primary and preferred fuel for all types of exercise, regardless of intensity... carbohydrate is the body's preferred fuel at all exercise intensities.
findings.truth: At rest and at low intensity fat supplies most of the energy; carbohydrate becomes dominant as intensity rises. The lesson's own next paragraph says fat is the low-intensity fuel, so the two passages contradicted each other. Five edits across content, conclusion, a knowledge-check option and a flashcard.
findings.evidence: substrate-use physiology; the lesson's own fat paragraph

findings.claim: Every banded mark scheme in this unit uses Mastering / Secure / Developing / Emerging as band names.
findings.truth: These are not the house band names (Top band / Upper-mid band / Mid band / Lower-mid band / Low band), but they are not on the banned-string list either, and they run across the whole PE build and probably other subjects. Options: leave them and change them in a subject-wide sweep, or rename here and accept that this unit reads differently from its neighbours.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned-string rule
findings.ruling: NOTE: band names left for the programme-wide band-ladder sweep.

findings.claim: Lesson descriptions in L4, L6, L8, L10, L12 and L13 run to 101-106 characters.
findings.truth: The validator limit is under 100 characters. Nothing in them is wrong, so no edit was made, but the unit will trip a length check if one runs over every field.

summary: The unit's content is spec-accurate on the things that matter most: two skill continua only, SMART with Recorded, the three OCR PEDs, guidance and feedback types the right way round, the seven components of a balanced diet, and every knowledge-check answer key correct. The damage is an exam-format fault repeated across seven lessons - an 8-mark evaluate question and matching exam tips that this paper never sets - plus three spec-scope slips (injury missing from the eight physical health items, a closed list of six sedentary consequences, carbohydrate called the preferred fuel at all intensities) and two arithmetic or example errors.
